title: ansible
summary: Ansible is a long-running British science fiction fanzine edited by Dave Langford, here represented by a sequence of issues spanning roughly 1982 to 1995. Its contents are a mix of news, gossip, and commentary about the SF field, fandom, and publishing, written in a witty, irreverent and often self-deprecating voice. The excerpts include convention reports from Novacon and Fencon, with accounts of panels, auctions, parties and misbehaviour; a tribute to the late Kingsley Amis; and short items on authors' disputes, obituaries, awards such as the Nebulas, small-press magazines, fan trivia and club notices. Later issues carry practical listings of fan contacts, convention bids, websites and back-issue archives. The newsletter is known for its compact, cross-referenced style, its running jokes and its cheerful gossip. Its archive is valued as a record of British fandom and the genre scene of the period, and as an example of the fannish newsletter tradition.
